value.rationale: The Plucker coordinate query class is canonical for finite Grassmannians and punctured projective systems; the complete first three nontrivial rank-two binary projections reveal nonpurity and explicit facet graph strata invisible to dimension/count and codeword weight. The six-coordinate double-star, disjoint triangle, theta and bipartite facets, together with two homology degrees, offer a motivated sharp finite benchmark and potential boundary data for larger Grassmannians. An exact small-order classification is valuable without a paper-sized all-n theorem.
